## The failing lines

### F-1 (lines 2, 3, 4): "of a holed face a graph with h cycles" holds only where every ring keeps about half a step from the others

**Evidence (CONFIRMED, executed).** `probe-claims.mts` runs `medialAxis(rings, 100)` over M0-a-11's §13.1 holed polygons
(`holedPolygons(seed, 1000)`, `packages/kernel/test/skeleton/support.ts`), judged by the item's own `topology()`,
`insideEvenOdd()` and `meet()` (`test/medial/support.ts`):

| face set | faces | cycles ≠ h | components ≠ 1 | node outside | arc meeting a ring |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| holed polygons, seed 1 | 1 000 | **80** | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| holed polygons, seed 2 | 1 000 | **79** | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| holed polygons, seed 3 | 1 000 | **81** | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| the corpus's courtyards (h = 1) | 196 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Every failure has fewer cycles than holes (seed 1 #9: 3 holes, 2 cycles; seed 3 #29: 4 holes, 2 cycles). `probe-cause.mts`:
on seed 1 the least gap between two rings is 50 cm in all 80 failures (min = median = max = 50), while 111 passing sets
also have a gap under 1 m; all 80 regain their h cycles at a 25 cm step (and at 10 cm). So a loop is lost where a hole
lies within about half a step of another ring (CONFIRMED). The mechanism is PLAUSIBLE, not traced edge by edge: the 1 m
samples' Delaunay triangles across the gap have circumcentres beyond the far wall, and the edges ending there are
dropped by the `inside` test, which opens the loop.

The author's own fixture shows it. `axis.test.ts` 256 – 257 (the narrow-passage test) builds a hole 30 cm from the outer
ring at 0° and at 23°; `probe-evidence.mts` on those exact rings:

```
hole 30 cm from the outer ring, 0° {"components":1,"cycles":1,"nodes":90,"arcs":90}
hole 30 cm from the outer ring, 23° {"components":1,"cycles":0,"nodes":95,"arcs":94}
```

That test asserts only `nodes.length > 1`, `checkInside` and `checkCanonical` (axis.test.ts 263 – 268), so the lost loop
passes. The h-cycle test (axis.test.ts 147 – 175) draws holes 500 – 900 cm wide on a 1 500 cm pitch with a 500 cm end
margin — no ring comes near another. C-0172 (5) states "walls facing each other and every hole's loop stay; so … a holed
face's has one cycle per hole", which these runs refute; no row declares the limit.

**Required change** (either):
(a) make the claim hold — e.g. sample more densely where two rings come within a step of each other (a choices row
naming §3.8's "at 1 m" as the default step and the local refinement), then test cycles = h on M0-a-11's holed polygons
at the checker's three seeds and on the 23° case; or
(b) declare the limit in a new choices row (a hole within about half a step + 1 cm of another ring may lose its loop at
that passage — the passage §9.3's maximum-clearance spanning tree would drop first — measured 80 / 79 / 81 of 1 000 on
the holed polygons, all restored at 25 cm), correct C-0172 (5)'s sentence by that row, and test exactly the declared
property: cycles = h whenever every ring gap is at least the stated bound (on M0-a-11's holed polygons, three seeds),
and the 23° case pinned as a declared loss.

### F-2 (lines 2, 4): the pruning splits the axis of a face without holes — 216 of the 2 000 corpus faces

**Evidence (CONFIRMED, executed).** `probe-claims.mts` over the committed corpus (`loadCorpus()`): 216 of 2 000 faces
give an axis with 2 or 3 components (notched 92, quad 81, rectilinear 33, irregular 6, compound 4; courtyards and bent
bars 0); none has a node outside or an arc meeting a ring. Corpus face 9 (a notched footprint):

```
corpus face 9 (family notched): medial {"components":3,"cycles":0,"nodes":27,"arcs":24} skeleton skeleton
```

The cause is the π × clearance rule (C-0172 (5)), not the step: a 25 cm step reconnects 4 of the 216; an instrumented
copy of `axis.ts` (`axis-probe.mts`, the ratio as a parameter) leaves 216 split at 2.5, 207 at 2, 79 at 1.5, 36 at 1.2
and 18 at 1; on face 9, 174 edges are dropped as outside and 82 by the ratio. The test "a face with no hole is a tree"
(axis.test.ts 177 – 191) asserts one component on four hand-picked shapes (an L, a T, a U, a triangle). C-0172 (5)
declares that the rule removes the branches of corners above about 79° and keeps the rest; it names no interior edge
removed and no split. §9.3 processes the sampled medial axis "the same way" as the skeleton — a maximum-clearance
spanning tree and the longest path of that tree — which a forest does not give.

**Required change** (either):
(a) make the pruning keep the axis connected — e.g. refuse a pruning that disconnects the graph or opens a hole's loop
(remove branches from their boundary end inward only) — recorded in a choices row superseding C-0172 (5)'s rule, with a
test over the whole corpus (components = 1, cycles = h) beside the four shapes; or
(b) declare the split in a choices row with its measured rate (216 / 2 000, by family) and name how a `spine` reader takes
a forest (staged to the milestone that builds §9.3, with its §4b or choices entry), and replace the "tree" test's title
and claim by the declared property, tested over the corpus.

### F-3 (line 2): two promises with no test that can fail — the per-file outside-plat refusal and §3.8's 1 m step

**Evidence (CONFIRMED, executed; mutant table below).** R9 deletes `loadCorpus`'s per-file refusal
(`runner.ts` 107, `if (!insidePlat(real)) throw …`) and every test stays green (`Tests  21 passed (21)`): only the folder's
refusal is tested ("refuses a corpus folder that resolves outside plat/ before reading anything in it"), while C-0172 (9)
promises that `loadCorpus` "resolves every path and refuses one outside plat/ before reading it". The lint's
whole-tree check refuses a committed symbolic link out of `plat/` (`tools/lint/paths.mjs` (1)), but not one made between
lint runs, which is what the runner's guard is for. X14c sets `MEDIAL_STEP_CM` to 80 and all 50 tests stay green;
200 and 150 (X14, X14b) are caught only by one counterexample's incidental `expect(axis.nodes.length).toBeGreaterThan(100)`
(axis.test.ts 312). No test pins §3.8's "boundary samples at 1 m" — every bar in `axis.test.ts` scales with
`STEP = MEDIAL_STEP_CM`, and `MedialAxis.sites` is never asserted.

## Notes (not failing lines)

* **N-1** (spec). `M0-work.json`'s `timingBars` row for the skeleton median says its miss takes "one repair pass, then the
  downgrades become the defaults (§3.8)", while C-0098 puts "the skeleton median" on the ordered ladder and asks every
  kernel row's `miss` column to carry that one form; M0.md §1 (a) follows C-0098, and so does the item's
  `SKELETON_TIMING_ROW.changeOnMiss`. The twin's row is stale; for the session's spec lane.
* **N-2** (spec). C-0026 lists "§3.8's downgrades-as-default" among the configuration fallbacks "still built as a switch
  and tested at M0"; this item's brief defers it "only on a measured corpus miss after one repair pass (§3.8; C-0026)",
  M0-a-11's `SkeletonOptions` has no such switch and §4b has no row. The item follows its brief; the conflict is the
  spec's, for the session.
* **N-3** (test strictness). `checkCanonical` (axis.test.ts 59 – 63) asserts node order in world coordinates, but C-0172
  (6) sorts in the local frame and then adds the integer corner; a sub-ulp near-tie can swap after the shift. Mutant D5
  (a one-ulp change of |b − a|²) failed the holed and narrow-passage tests on that assertion alone. Either assert the
  local-frame order or declare the world order.
* **N-4** (equivalent survivors, one line each, no test needed): A5, X3, X18 and X7 — each line in the mutant table.
* **N-5** (another item). M0-a-11's `translation.test.ts` takes ≈ 3.5 s alone and timed out at vitest's default 5 s
  under load 18.6; informative for its owner, not this item's.
